savings_opportunities.opportunity: Council Tax: Empty Homes + Second Homes premium revenue capture (LURA 2023)
savings_opportunities.evidence: Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023 s.79 reduces the long-term-empty dwelling threshold from 2 years to 1 year (effective 1 April 2024 for financial years 2024/25 onwards). LURA 2023 s.80 enables billing authorities to apply a 100% premium on second homes effective 1 April 2025 (subject to local resolution). Bradford 223,592 dwellings; even a conservative 0.5-1% empty dwelling rate (1,100-2,200 dwellings) at 100% premium on Band C average GBP 1,500 = GBP 1.7m to GBP 3.3m gross revenue. Conservative sizing: capture 30-40% of that gross.

savings_opportunities.opportunity: DSG High Needs Block sustainability and Safety Valve readiness
savings_opportunities.evidence: DSG statutory override in force to March 2026 (extension pending). National pattern: 60%-plus of upper-tier LAs run HNB deficits; Bradford caseload places it in the high-volume tier. The override removes the requirement to charge HNB deficit against the general fund. If removed without DSG funding settlement, Bradford carries a material GF subsidy. Safety Valve programme (DfE, 2020 onwards) provides additional funding in return for an improvement plan; Surrey, Hertfordshire and 30-plus LAs are signatories. Bradford has not been a Safety Valve signatory to date.

Bradford 0-17 population 142,483, one of the largest in England; demand-side scale is substantial.

LCC's equivalent lever (H+T lever 6, Section 38/278 developer contributions) sizes GBP 0.6m to GBP 1.5m at LCC scale. Bradford holds local planning + Section 106 / CIL discretion (LCC does not). Bradford has the wider unitary scope so the actual ceiling could be higher; conservative pro-rata at 60%.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Planning Act 2008 + Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010; Town and Country Planning Act 1990 s.106; Highways Act 1980 ss.38, 278

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Highways Asset Management Plan whole-life-cost efficiency
savings_opportunities.evidence: LCC's equivalent lever (H+T lever 4, Asset management / pothole programme efficiency) sizes GBP 0.6m to GBP 1.5m at LCC scale. Bradford-pro-rata at 60% (Bradford's highways estate is smaller than LCC's 7,168 road miles). Whole-life-cost methodology: preventative maintenance vs reactive repair; surface treatment timing; pothole-prevention through better-quality first-time repair.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Highways Act 1980 s.41 (highway maintenance); UK Roads Liaison Group code of practice

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Active travel + DfT grant capture (revenue offset for cycling + walking infrastructure)
savings_opportunities.evidence: LCC's equivalent lever (H+T lever 5, Active travel grant capture) sizes GBP 0.4m to GBP 1.0m at LCC scale. Bradford-pro-rata at 60%. Active Travel England funding (formerly capital-only) now permits modest revenue offset for promotion + behaviour-change programmes; WYCA-aligned LCWIP (Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan) captures.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Transport Act 2000 + Local Transport Act 2008; Active Travel England (gov department since 2022)

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Roadworks operator concentration + permit scheme efficiency
savings_opportunities.evidence: LCC's equivalent lever (H+T lever 1, Roadworks operator concentration) sizes GBP 1m to GBP 3m at LCC scale. Bradford has multiple statutory undertakers (Northern Gas Networks + Yorkshire Water + utility providers) operating in the highway. Roadworks permit scheme + lane rental + traffic management cost recovery + operator-concentration via NRSWA s.74 + Traffic Management Act 2004 Part 3.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: New Roads and Street Works Act 1991 s.74; Traffic Management Act 2004 Part 3 + Schedule 4A

directorates._note: 12 statutory functions LCC does not hold. Balfour Beatty Civil GBP 41.1m / 209 txns highways relationship. Muse Developments GBP 31.4m / 27 txns (regen capital build). Largest LCC-mentoring scope gap (housing, planning, homelessness).

directorates.name: Neighbourhoods and Community Safety

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Licensing fee full cost recovery (alcohol + entertainment + taxi)
savings_opportunities.evidence: Licensing service GBP 122k visible (MHCLG RO 24/25 sub-line). Likely a much larger gross-cost figure netted against fee income. Fee structure is set under regulations; cost-recovery audit + fee uplift on chargeable services yields 15-25% typical.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Licensing Act 2003 + Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976

savings_opportunities.opportunity: CCTV estate consolidation + WY Police partnership
savings_opportunities.evidence: CCTV MHCLG RO sub-line GBP 942k 24/25. Cameras + monitoring + maintenance + storage. Partnership models with WY Police (shared monitoring + shared maintenance contracts) yield 15-25% savings.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Crime and Disorder Act 1998 + Localism Act 2011 s.1

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Community grants programme review - outcome-focused + de-duplicate
savings_opportunities.evidence: Community development + safety MHCLG line GBP 7.28M 24/25. Significant grant footprint. Bradford has historically used community grants as cohesion + youth-diversion tool. Outcome-focused review + de-duplication yields 5-10% of the grant tail.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Localism Act 2011 s.1

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Fly-tipping enforcement uplift - cost-recovery on FPN
savings_opportunities.evidence: Street cleansing line GBP 7.07M 24/25; fly-tipping clearance is a major sub-cost. National pattern: enforcement-led councils issue 100-500 FPN per 100,000 population; recovery rate 30-50%.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Environmental Protection Act 1990 s.33 + Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Trading standards + regulatory cost recovery
savings_opportunities.evidence: LCC's equivalent lever (REC lever 5, Trading standards + regulatory cost recovery) sizes GBP 0.2m to GBP 0.5m at LCC scale. Bradford trading standards function is in Bradford's portfolio. Cost-recovery on commercial complaints + statutory regulation + Proceeds of Crime Act enforcement.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Consumer Rights Act 2015 + Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 s.78 (asset recovery incentive scheme)

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Volunteer-supported community delivery (libraries, sport, environmental volunteering)
savings_opportunities.evidence: LCC's equivalent lever (Civic Pride lever 6, Volunteer-supported community delivery) sizes GBP 0.1m to GBP 0.3m at LCC scale. Bradford VCSE sector + 62% minority school cohort = community-volunteer base. Cross-portfolio with HPP libraries lever.
savings_opportunities.vires_citation: Volunteer Centres + Local Government Act 1972 (general powers)

directorates._note: Smallest portfolio by 28/29 ceiling. Mostly statutory pass-through (WY Fire GBP 48.7m + Police precept GBP 32.0m via OPCC).

mtfs_gap_cumulative._capitalisation_direction_note: The £570m figure previously recorded here was the March 2025 PLANNED profile across seven years, not a total already drawn. The revised profile is £391m across four years (2023/24 to 2026/27) and ends after 2026/27. The 2025/26 direction fell from a £127.1m ceiling to £113m because £14.1m of in-year underspend was applied to it. Source: Revenue Outturn 2025-26, Table 13, report to the Executive of 9 June 2026, bradford.moderngov.co.uk. Supersedes the March 2025 MTFS profile (Doc AY).

risks.risk: MHCLG Best Value Notice LAPSED 27 February 2025 and was not reissued. No commissioners were appointed; an independent Improvement Panel and CIPFA assurance reviews run as a condition of Exceptional Financial Support. No Section 114 notice has ever been issued. The external auditor still reports significant weaknesses in value-for-money arrangements, on financial sustainability and children's services governance (Forvis Mazars, 10 Feb 2026).
ASC and Children's Social Care structural pressures of about GBP 18m and GBP 38m per year respectively (2025-2030 MTFS, Doc AY).

Dedicated Schools Grant account closed 2025/26 in SURPLUS at £16.2m, down £8.4m, because High Needs spend came in below forecast. It is forecast into deficit at c£48.65m by March 2027 and above £100m by March 2028 on a nothing-changes basis, driven by a forecast £48.5m in-year High Needs overspend in 2026/27 after DfE suspended the national High Needs funding uplift. Bradford is in neither Safety Valve nor Delivering Better Value, and Safety Valve is closing nationally. The statutory override ceases 1 April 2028.

Bradford Children and Families Trust delivered a balanced outturn against its £212.4m contract sum in 2025/26 (£6.8m staffing underspend offset by a £9.0m placements overspend) and has £20.0m of savings proposals for 2026/27 against a c£206.5m contract sum. Ofsted rated it Requires Improvement to be Good in January 2026, up from Inadequate. Children's social care remains c£60m above benchmark spend comparators.
Reform UK runs Bradford as a minority administration (29 of 90 seats); Cabinet decisions are subject to opposition call-in, so the programme needs issue-by-issue majorities.
Financial-recovery scrutiny pressure from the opposition benches on every savings decision.
